transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-21 | Time: 10:00 AM PT | Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Redwood CSM); Priya Rao (Asteria Head of AI), Tom Bishop (Infra Lead), Leah Kim (Security), Marcus Chen (Product)

Summary: quick POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling for a search & assistant use case; agree success criteria (latency, throughput, cost), get sample traces, run baseline benchmarks on Redwood hosted and Dedicated options, timeline for Nov POC.

Topics: workload QPS and concurrency, input/output token distributions, long-context vs short queries, success metrics (95th p99 latency targets), benchmarks (throughput runs), networking/security (VPC, KMS, SOC2), timeline and next steps.

[00:00] Samantha: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intro - I'm Samantha, AE on the Redwood side, and Carlos is our systems engineer. we'll run through scoping for the POC focused on workload modeling.

[00:27] Priya: thanks Samantha, excited to dig in - short background, we're building an internal assistant + retrieval layer for advisors, mix of short Q/A and long doc summarization. we expect spikes during market open.

[00:45] Carlos: great, can you give ballpark QPS and avg tokens per request? even rough numbers help us size.

[00:57] Marcus: most queries are short, maybe 40 to 120 tokens input and 30 to 80 tokens output, but we have a tail where users submit a 3k to 4k context for deep summarize, that's maybe 5-10% of calls.

[01:15] Tom: traffic wise avg day QPS is small now, ~8 qps, but peak open-of-day could hit 65-80 qps for a 10-15 minute burst. concurrency around 40 at peak assuming some batching.

[01:35] Carlos: ok that's super helpful. so for sizing we usually model steady-state qps and peak burst. for a POC we can run synthetic load to emulate your 80 qps bursts and the 4k-context cases. do you have traces?

[01:55] Priya: we can export a 7-day trace, yes. Tom will send.

[02:02] Tom: yep I'll export sample payloads and the trace.

[02:10] Samantha: perfect. Success criteria - what would you consider a win?

[02:20] Priya: three things: 1) 95th percentile latency under 300 to 350 ms for short queries, 2) ability to sustain 80 qps burst without >5% error, and 3) predictable unit cost - we'd like to see cost per 1M tokens below our internal threshold, which is roughly $2k for production targets but POC is flexible. also security requirements for the POC - SOC2 + SSO + KMS integration.

[02:55] Leah: on security, we need to verify data residency controls, audit logs and customer-managed key support - is that possible in the POC? we can do limited data in hosted but prefer VPC for production.

[03:12] Carlos: short answer yes - for POC we can do hosted with private VPC peering or a dedicated pool depending on timeline. note: our private plane (sic) can be set up but provisioning Dedicated GPUs can take a few weeks. for the POC we usually run on Redwood hosted with strict retention and KMS integration for the ingest path.

[03:38] Priya: ok that makes sense. curious about caching and batching - you mentioned KV cache on the docs but sometimes it's K-V cash in transcripts, but how does that play into cost and latency?

[03:55] Carlos: yeah sorry audio transcribe - our runtime supports prefix and KV cache; for repeated context (like repeated access to same document) we can cache KV states and reduce token compute. that helps especially for long-context sessions to reduce per-token latency and cost. for your mix where 90% short queries and 10% long contexts, we can likely see ~20-30% unit cost savings if caching is effective.

[04:25] Marcus: what's the expected throughput impact with caching?

[04:30] Carlos: depends on the hit-rate; in bench runs we instrumented typical retrieval stacks and saw 1.5x to 3x effective throughput for cached hot paths. but for cold long-context requests you still pay the full cost.

[04:48] Samantha: let's talk benchmarks - Carlos, what's the bench plan for this POC?

[04:54] Carlos: we'll run two phases. Phase A: profile your sample traffic (short + tail) on hosted API to validate latency and p95/p99 under synthetic load. Phase B: endurance run 24h with representative distribution to catch memory leaks, kv-cache behavior, and throughput consistency. we'll also run a dedicated-config test if you want Dedicated sizing. deliverables: latency percentiles, throughput graphs, token counts, error rates, and cost estimates per million tokens.

[05:25] Priya: timeline question - how fast can we get the Phase A baseline?

[05:30] Samantha: if we get traces this week, Carlos can kick off a baseline run next week - target baseline week of Nov 2. Phase B can run the following week. final POC report and demo by Nov 20, roughly a three-week cadence.

[05:48] Tom: any infra changes needed? e.g., VPC peering or firewall opening?

[05:55] Carlos: for hosted bench nothing special beyond sample payloads and an IP allow-list if you want restricted ingestion. for VPC or private deployment we'll need a network window for peering or an on-prem agent; that adds ~2-3 weeks.

[06:10] Leah: about encryption - we run with customer-managed keys (KMS). is the key rotation supported for the ingest pipeline?

[06:18] Carlos: yes, we integrate with KMS/HSM providers; for POC we can demo with a test key and show rotation patterns, and we'll provide our security pack with specifics.

[06:30] Marcus: cost model - can you give a rough cost delta between hosted and Dedicated for our workload?

[06:36] Samantha: quick rough: Hosted is usage-based so immediate but unit cost higher under heavy sustained load; Dedicated is lower per-token at scale but requires a commit. for your numbers (peak bursts, moderate sustained) we can run model to show break-even. Carlos will include a cost projection in the bench report.

[06:58] Tom: what about latency SLOs - can Redwood hit p95 300 ms for a 512-token model? our short queries are sub-150 tokens typically.

[07:10] Carlos: for short queries sub-150 tokens on our optimized kernels we routinely hit p95 ~150-220 ms depending on model variant. p99 could be higher. we'll test your exact model/config. note that sequence length and batch size change kernel selection - we'll surface that in the report.

[07:35] Priya: models - we plan to start with an open model for cost reasons, maybe a quantized 33B variant. can Redwood support quantized model variants and do benchmarks?

[07:48] Carlos: yes, we support quantized execution paths. we also recommend a few model variants that balance latency and quality. we'll propose model profiles in the SOW, and run the same traffic across 2-3 model candidates.

[08:05] Samantha: transcript note: sometimes the auto-transcribe mangles names, so we'll make sure delivered artifacts are clean.

[08:12] Leah: one more security note: we need audit logs for every request in POC. is that feasible?

[08:20] Carlos: we can deliver request-level audit logs for the POC with redacted PII; for production we support longer retention windows as an add-on. we'll include sample log exports.

[08:36] Marcus: ok great. on the success criteria you mentioned error rate under 5% during bursts - what's typical?

[08:44] Carlos: for well-provisioned hosted runs we see <1% transient errors; sustained errors often point to networking or malformed payloads. we'll instrument retries and fallbacks (model variant fallback) as part of the test.

[09:05] Priya: can we also validate cost per 1M tokens with and without caching? that would help our finance team.

[09:12] Samantha: yes we'll do both baseline and cache-enabled runs and report per-million token estimates.

[09:20] Tom: what telemetry do you need from our side?

[09:24] Carlos: ideally: 7-day traffic trace with timestamps and payload sizes, samples of worst-case long-context payloads, authentication method for API calls (service account), and any network allow-list endpoints. that will let us replay realistic traffic.

[09:40] Tom: i'll get that to you by Friday.

[09:45] Samantha: thanks. recap of next steps: Samantha to send SOW and pricing, Carlos to run baseline bench once traces are in, Tom to share traces, Leah to confirm compliance contact, and we'll target Nov 2 for the baseline.

[09:59] Priya: sounds good. one minor nit: when you say "Redwood Dedicated" the team sometimes hears "red wood dedicated" in notes, so pls make sure the naming is clear in docs.

[10:10] Carlos: noted, we'll standardize names. also we'll include a to-be-run checklist so POC runs smoothly.

[10:20] Marcus: any other outstanding asks?

[10:25] Leah: if you can include a sample template for the traffic trace that would be awesome.

[10:30] Samantha: will do. thanks everyone - we'll follow up with SOW and security pack.

[10:36] (crosstalk) Priya: thanks all.

END OF TRANSCRIPT
